findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either add an AC for the post-re-enable final sweep (or explicitly hand it to a named follow-up ticket) so the durable-removal end-state is reachable and verified.
evidence: 'They will be re-posted once, then deduped from pass 2 onward.'
'a final sweep after the first pass is planned rather than improvised' — but no AC asserts the sweep occurs or verifies post-re-enable state.
findings.finding: The plan states a final sweep after the first re-enabled bridge pass is 'planned', but no acceptance criterion covers that sweep, so the durable-removal end-state is not reachable within this ticket's ACs.
scenarios: Operator completes all ACs (deletes + canary + keep-one), re-enables bridge, comments re-post, and no criterion drives the follow-up sweep to remove them.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Document the restore procedure from the pre-deletion backup (how to re-post deleted comments) and note whether re-post fidelity/authorship is achievable.
evidence: Backup existence is gated ('gated on len(fetched) == total') but the plan never states how a wrongful deletion would be restored from the payload.
T4 remedy requires an explicit rollback mechanism, not merely an acknowledgement/backup artifact.
findings.finding: Deletion of Jira comments is irreversible, and while a pre-deletion backup is required, no restore/back-out procedure from that backup is described.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'Pre-deletion backup of the full comment payload'
scenarios: The canary or a keep-one assertion reveals an over-deletion after DELETEs have executed on REB-2605.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify (and dry-run test on the canary) the restore procedure that re-creates deleted comments from the pre-deletion backup, so the backup is a tested undo path and not just an archived artifact.
evidence: Plan states 'deletion is irreversible' and requires a backup gated on 'len(fetched) == total', but no AC or step describes re-posting/restoring from that backup.
Canary on REB-2605 verifies before proceeding, but if verification fails after deletion, the only undo asset is the backup — whose replay procedure is unspecified.
findings.finding: The plan establishes an irreversible operation (Jira comment DELETE) and creates a pre-deletion backup, but never specifies the RESTORE path — how a deleted comment would actually be re-created from the backup payload if the canary or a post-canary step reveals an error. The backup is a reversibility artifact with no defined, tested undo procedure.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria: 'Pre-deletion backup of the full comment payload for each affected issue exists before any DELETE'
scenarios: Canary deletes 138 comments on REB-2605, post-deletion re-fetch reveals a keep-one violation (a distinct body was dropped); operator has the backup JSON but no defined way to restore the mistakenly-deleted comment, so recovery is improvised under pressure.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: 'A restore step re-posts comments from the backup payload; it is dry-run-verified on the canary issue (post backup, before any real deletion) so the undo path is proven, not improvised.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate concretely what counts as an 'ambiguous case' (e.g. tied created-timestamps for the oldest copy, missing created field) so the skip rule is deterministic.
evidence: The four-condition rule is fully conjunctive, so it is unclear what residual 'ambiguity' the criterion contemplates.
No definition of an ambiguous case is given
findings.finding: The 'Ambiguous cases are SKIPPED and reported' criterion does not define what makes a case ambiguous.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'Ambiguous cases are SKIPPED and reported'
scenarios: A comment that meets 3 of 4 conditions, or a body that is length 32767 but lacks a clear oldest copy (tied timestamps).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the deployment ordering between 5931's marker-order fix and the bridge re-enable, and specify which identification rule the post-pass-1 final sweep uses in each case (four-condition rule if 5931 is not yet live; marker/dedup if it is).
evidence: Plan: 'They will be re-posted once, then deduped from pass 2 onward.'
Plan: 'a final sweep after the first pass is planned rather than improvised.'
5931 (unreal-empathetic-illadopsis) is 'open' / planning — its fix (reserve room for the marker before truncating) is not yet shipped.

Verified in code: _decorate_outbound_comment returns f'{body}\n\n{RECONCILER_MARKER}' and truncate_comment_body cuts to 32767 dropping the trailing marker — so until 5931 lands, any re-posted over-length comment is STILL marker-less and only the four-condition rule (not the marker rule) can identify it.
findings.finding: The 'final sweep after the first pass' relies on an unstated deployment ordering: whether the 5931 marker-order fix is live BEFORE the bridge is re-enabled determines whether the single expected re-post carries the marker (auto-deduped / marker-cleanable) or is again marker-less (requiring another four-condition sweep). The plan does not state this dependency.
findings.location: Sequencing hazard section + AC 'a final sweep after the first pass is planned'
scenarios: Bridge re-enabled while 5931 is still unfixed: the one expected re-post is marker-less, so the 'final sweep' must itself run the four-condition rule, not the phase-1 marker rule.
5931 ships first: the re-post carries the marker and is caught by normal dedup / marker-based tooling, and the sweep may be unnecessary.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Sequencing hazard section: 'If the bridge is re-enabled before 5931 ships, the single re-post is still marker-less and the final sweep MUST re-apply the four-condition rule; if 5931 ships first, the re-post carries the marker and is handled by normal dedup.'

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make cleanup.py inspectable to the review (vendor it into the repo, or paste the --include-truncated candidate predicate) so a reviewer can confirm it enforces all four conjunctive conditions — including the exact len==32767 check — before the dry run and canary are trusted.
evidence: list_directory of repo root shows no jira-cleanup-20260820/ and the path escapes the repository root (read_file returned 'path escapes the repository root'), so the tool is unverifiable from here
The claim is the crux: the whole cleanup (dry run + canary + deletions) runs through this tool under --include-truncated
The plan attributes condition 2 (exact-length) as 'added after the earlier dry run', which is a specific implementation-state claim that cannot be confirmed
Discrimination rule: external artifact outside tool reach → covered-but-unverifiable rather than a refuted codebase exclusion
findings.finding: The load-bearing execution-tool assertion — 'The tightened rule [all four conditions] is already implemented in /Users/joeoakhart/jira-cleanup-20260820/cleanup.py behind --include-truncated; the exact-length check (condition 2) was added after the earlier dry run' — cannot be verified: cleanup.py lives at an absolute path OUTSIDE this repo root, so repo-scoped Read/Grep cannot confirm the tool exists or that it enforces all four conjunctive conditions. Every other codebase assertion in the plan (RECONCILER_MARKER value, _TRUNCATION_SUFFIX, exact-32767 length, _record_comment_id no-backfill, and the 5931 truncation-order defect) was confirmed against live code.
findings.location: Identification rule — 'The tightened rule is already implemented in /Users/joeoakhart/jira-cleanup-20260820/cleanup.py behind --include-truncated'
scenarios: cleanup.py's --include-truncated actually applies only 3 of the 4 conditions (e.g. omits or loosens condition 2/4), so the dry-run 'candidate count' reflects a broader-than-intended population and a keep-one or non-candidate comment is deleted
The tool at that path differs from the reviewed rule (drift between the plan's stated rule and the binary that runs)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the exact body-normalization used for keep-one grouping (which text field, and what transforms).
evidence: 'for each distinct normalized body the OLDEST copy survives'
The body never defines what normalization is applied (whitespace? marker-strip? the pre-strip vs post-strip rendered text)
findings.finding: The keep-one criterion depends on a 'normalized body' but the normalization procedure is never defined in the plan.
scenarios: Two copies differ only by trailing whitespace or a stripped marker — do they count as the same normalized body or distinct?
findings.suggested_fix: State that grouping uses the pre-strip rendered ADF text with the RECONCILER_MARKER stripped and trailing whitespace trimmed, matching phase 1's grouping key.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify DELETE-loop error handling: per-comment result logging, behavior on rate-limit/network error (retry/backoff), and safe resumption after partial completion.
evidence: The plan performs many DELETE calls per issue (~138 on REB-2605) against the Jira API but does not describe error handling, partial-failure recovery, or per-delete logging.
No mention of what happens if the run is interrupted after some deletions.
findings.finding: The DELETE loop's failure handling and idempotency are unspecified: no statement of behavior on a mid-issue API failure, retry/backoff, or re-running after partial completion.
scenarios: Network error or rate-limit mid-issue leaves an issue partially cleaned; operator re-runs the tool.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC that the pre-deletion backup is verified RESTORABLE (a rehearsed restore/re-post path for a deleted comment) and that the DELETE run is idempotent/resumable after partial failure (already-deleted ids skipped, keep-one recomputed safely on re-run).
evidence: AC: 'Pre-deletion backup of the full comment payload for each affected issue exists before any DELETE, gated on len(fetched) == total' — asserts existence, not restorability
Deletion is irreversible per the plan ('deletion is irreversible'); the backup is the only stated back-out artifact
T11 ROLLBACK/DATA-LOSS requires 'a back-out path and no data loss on partial failure' — a back-out that can report success while leaving state unrecoverable is the named risk
No stated idempotency/resume behavior for a DELETE run interrupted partway (e.g., re-running after failure on one issue)
findings.finding: The plan mandates a pre-deletion backup exists (gated on len(fetched)==total) but never asserts that backup is RESTORABLE — there is no restore/re-post procedure verifying a wrongly-deleted comment can be recreated from the backup, and no idempotency/resume guard on the DELETE loop so a mid-run failure can be safely re-run without double-counting.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'Pre-deletion backup ... exists before any DELETE' and canary line
scenarios: Canary or a later issue partially deletes, then the run aborts; operator re-runs and the loop re-processes already-deleted ids or mis-computes keep-one
A comment is deleted in error and the operator must reconstruct it from the backup but no restore path was rehearsed

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the Jira auth/permission precondition explicitly (bot accountId 712020:6471376f… holds the project 'Delete all comments' permission, confirmed by the canary DELETE) and specify that a 403 on DELETE aborts the issue rather than being treated as idempotent-404 success.
evidence: Repo verify (MATCH): acli_graph.py:563-571 delete_comment -> DELETE /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment/{id}, 'Probe-validated: returns 204 on success.'
Auth transport is Basic-over-HTTPS per sibling review (acli_rest _direct_rest_delete); permission is a separate project grant.

The sibling 76b2 plan-review cache (.rebar/cache/plan-review/76b2-4b5f-5682-45e5/d14503de...json) raised this exact gap for the identical DELETE integration: '403 (insufficient permission) is a different failure than the idempotent 404'.

ABSENCE: no plan text asserts the bot holds delete-comment permission; the canary AC ('execute on REB-2605 alone, verify it fully') checks deletion outcome, not a permission pre-flight, and no AC line distinguishes 403 from 404.
Evidence class: DELETE endpoint = Verified; delete-permission for the bot token = Unverified.
findings.finding: The plan depends on Jira comment DELETE succeeding across ~836 calls but states no auth/permission precondition (T3 check c) and no handling for a 403 distinct from the idempotent 404. The DELETE endpoint exists (verified: acli_graph.py:563 DELETE /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment/{id}, '204 on success'), but endpoint existence does not imply the bot accountId is granted the project 'Delete all comments' permission; the bot is proven able to POST comments (that is what produced the duplicates) yet delete permission is an orthogonal server-side grant.
scenarios: The bot token can POST (proven) but was never granted 'Delete all comments' on the target project; the very first canary DELETE on REB-2605 returns 403, blocking the operation after the backup pass.
A mid-run 403 is misclassified as the handled idempotent-404 case, silently under-deleting.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an auth/HTTPS precondition line to the Sequencing/Safety section — Basic-over-HTTPS with a token whose account holds delete-comment permission, verified on the REB-2605 canary — and add an AC that a 403 on DELETE stops execution (distinct from the idempotent-404 path).
